city_vars.market_blurb: Lufkin, Texas serves as the economic hub of Deep East Texas, historically anchored by the timber and wood products industry given its location in the Piney Woods. The city also has a strong manufacturing base tied to oilfield equipment production, along with healthcare and retail sectors that draw from surrounding rural counties. As the Angelina County seat, Lufkin functions as a regional commercial and medical center for much of East Texas.
city_vars.local_note: Much of Lufkin's housing stock consists of mid-20th-century single-family homes built on slab foundations, with newer subdivisions following similar construction. The dominant plumbing risk factor in this part of Texas is clay-soil slab leaks, as shifting soil conditions can stress slab plumbing lines over time.
city_vars.city_spotlight:
Lufkin sits at the heart of the Piney Woods, serving as the commercial anchor for Deep East Texas and the seat of Angelina County. The surrounding forests built the city's original economy, and timber and wood products manufacturing still run deep in its identity, though the modern base has broadened considerably. Lufkin Industries' oil field equipment work, alongside healthcare, education, retail, and government offices, now gives the local economy a sturdier, more diverse footing than its lumber-town roots alone.

With roughly 34,000 residents, Lufkin feels sized just right — big enough for full-service hospitals, a community college, and steady employers, yet small enough that neighborhoods like Crown Colony and Kurth still carry a distinct, close-knit character. It's a working city, proud of its piney landscape and its role as the region's steady hub.

columns.heading: No Hot Water
columns.text: A faulty pilot light, broken igniter, or gas supply issue often prevents your gas tank water heater from heating. Plumbing Connect links you with local providers who diagnose the cause and restore your hot water.

columns.heading: Water Leaking from Tank
columns.text: Corrosion, a failed anode rod, or internal tank damage can cause pooling water beneath your gas tank water heater. Contact a provider immediately—active leaks require urgent repair or replacement to prevent water damage.

columns.heading: Pilot Light Won't Stay Lit
columns.text: Mineral deposits, a worn thermocouple, or gas flow problems commonly cause the pilot to blow out on gas tank water heaters. Local providers Plumbing Connect connects you with can clean, adjust, or replace the faulty component.

columns.heading: Rotten Egg Smell
columns.text: Hydrogen sulfide odor from your gas tank water heater usually signals bacterial growth in the tank or anode rod corrosion. Providers diagnose the source and perform cleaning, anode replacement, or other gas tank water heater repair work.

columns.heading: Rusty or Discolored Water
columns.text: Sediment buildup or internal rust in your gas tank water heater degrades water quality and efficiency. Local providers can flush the tank, replace the anode rod, or recommend gas tank water heater replacement if damage is severe.

columns.heading: Strange Noises or Rumbling
columns.text: Sediment settling at the bottom of your gas tank water heater or a failing heating element creates popping and rumbling sounds. Plumbing Connect matches you with providers who flush the tank or perform gas tank water heater installation if replacement is needed.

fq_items.question: How should I prepare my home before gas tank water heater installation?
fq_items.answer: Clear the area around your water heater so the provider has safe access to work. Turn off your existing water heater before the appointment, and let the provider know of any space constraints or special setup in your home. Have your old unit's details available so the provider can recommend the right replacement size and type for your needs.

fq_items.question: What can I do to extend the life of a new gas tank water heater?
fq_items.answer: Flush your gas tank water heater annually to remove sediment buildup, check the pressure relief valve regularly, and have the system inspected periodically. These steps help it run efficiently and last longer. If you notice rust, leaks, or unusual noises, contact a provider promptly to prevent bigger problems.
